# CS-01 — Iron-triangle autopsy of a failed ERP rollout

!!! info "Case card"
    **Difficulty:** Beginner (CS-01..CS-20) ·
    **Level:** L1 — Single-concept drill ·
    **Domain:** D1 · **Seed project:** CAMPUSHUB

## Learning objectives

1. Represent project failure as a constraint conflict rather than a list of symptoms.
2. Distinguish observed facts from assumptions in a post-mortem.

## Project context

A mid-sized university signed a fixed-scope ERP replacement with a two-year window and a budget approved before requirements were baselined. Eighteen months in, the go-live has slipped twice, customizations have doubled, and the registrar refuses to retire the legacy system.

## Problem statement

The steering committee asks you to explain, in constraint terms, why the project is failing and which constraint is actually binding.

## Constraints and available information

- Use only the facts given; mark every inference as an assumption.
- Treat the iron triangle (scope, time, cost) plus quality as the four constraints.
- The budget was approved pre-requirements and has not been re-baselined.

## Student tasks

1. Draw the four-constraint diagram and place the observed symptoms on it.
2. Argue which single constraint is binding and what evidence supports that.
3. Name one trade-off decision the steering committee never explicitly made.

## Expected deliverables

- Constraint map (one page) with symptoms annotated.
- One-paragraph root-cause hypothesis with stated assumptions.

## Discussion questions

1. Can more than one constraint be binding at once? What does that imply?
1. Who should have surfaced the constraint conflict, and when?

## How you will be graded

Constraint map complete and correctly placed (40%); binding-constraint argument uses evidence, not opinion (40%); assumptions explicitly separated (20%).
